transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Taking care of my mom on top of work has thrown my whole life off, and I feel like I’m not handling any of it the way I usually would. Ever since her stroke, trying to balance everything has just been too much.
How long after your mom’s stroke did these feelings start, and have they lasted less than a month or longer than a month?

They started pretty quickly, within a few weeks of her stroke once I had to start juggling her hospital visits with my shifts at the shop. And it's definitely been longer than a month—this has been going on for about four months now.
Since these stress-related feelings started, have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself, or have you been unable to keep up with work or daily responsibilities because of them?

No, I don't have any thoughts of hurting myself, but I'm really struggling to keep up with my responsibilities. I actually had a scary near-miss safety incident at the shop because I was so distracted, and my supervisor has already warned me about my attitude with my coworkers. I've also had to completely drop out of church and my truck club because I'm just running on fumes.
Since your mom’s stroke, have you been feeling mostly sad, hopeless, or very anxious and worried most days?

I've been feeling completely overwhelmed and strung out trying to balance it all. I end up crying in the restroom at work between oil changes, and then I lie awake at night beating myself up because I feel like I'm dropping every single ball. It's just this constant, heavy stress and sadness that I can't seem to shake.
Have you noticed that these symptoms started within 3 months of your mom’s stroke and are mainly tied to that stressor, rather than happening without it?

Yes, absolutely. They started within just a few weeks of her stroke, right when I had to start juggling her care with my shifts at the shop. None of this was happening before, and it is completely tied to trying to handle this overwhelming situation.
Have these feelings and problems gone away at all when the stress is lighter, or do they stay present even during breaks from caregiving and work?

I haven't really had any breaks or lighter periods of stress over the last four months because the caregiving and work demands are completely constant. However, I keep telling myself that once my mom's health stabilizes and she doesn't need this level of care anymore, I'll be able to get back to my normal routine. I expect I'll stop feeling so strung out once things finally settle down.
Do you feel these symptoms would likely improve if your mom’s health and caregiving demands got better, or do you think they would keep going even after the stress is over?

I absolutely think they would get better. I keep telling myself that if and when my mom's health stabilizes and she doesn't need this level of care anymore, I'll be able to get back to my normal routine. I fully expect I'll stop feeling so strung out all the time once that weight is lifted.
Have these symptoms made it hard for you to function at work, at home, or in your relationships in a way that feels out of proportion to what you would normally expect from this stress?

Yes, it has completely derailed how I function day-to-day. I'm snapping at coworkers, crying in the shop restroom, and even had a dangerous near-miss at work because I was so distracted. I’ve also completely dropped out of my church and truck club, which is totally unlike me because those activities used to keep me grounded.
Have you had any thoughts of wanting to die, hurting yourself, or feeling that life is not worth living since this started?
No, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself or wanting to die at all. I am just feeling extremely overwhelmed and completely exhausted by this whole situation.
Have there been any other major stressors around the same time, or do your symptoms seem to be mainly a reaction to your mom’s stroke and the caregiving/work strain?

No, there aren't any other stressors in my life right now. Everything started when my mom had her stroke four months ago, and how I'm feeling is entirely a reaction to the sudden, overwhelming strain of caregiving on top of my demanding full-time job at the shop.
Besides feeling overwhelmed, have you also been feeling unusually sad, hopeless, or anxious most days since this started?

Yes, it feels like my whole life has been yanked inside out and I'm constantly anxious. I find myself crying in the restroom at work between oil changes, and then I lie awake at night beating myself up over everything. It is just a very heavy, sad feeling that I can't seem to shake.
Have you had any period during this time when the symptoms were much worse right after the stressor started and then began to ease up, or have they stayed at about the same level the whole time?

No, they haven't eased up at all. They have stayed consistently intense, if not worse, over the last four months because the caregiving demands are constant and never stop. The exhaustion has just kept building up, and I feel like I am constantly running on fumes.
Since this started, have you also noticed changes in your sleep, appetite, or energy that feel more than just being tired from being busy?

My sleep and energy have been completely wrecked. I lie awake at night beating myself up over everything I'm trying to manage, and I constantly feel like I'm running on fumes. I haven't really noticed any changes in my appetite, though, since I'm just so focused on the exhaustion.
Since this started, have you also lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy, or has it been more mainly feeling stressed, overwhelmed, and sad because of the situation?

It's not that I've lost interest in my truck club or church, because I really do miss them and want to go. I'm just so completely exhausted and overwhelmed by work and caregiving that I don't have the energy or the time to handle anything extra right now.
Have you ever had a time in the past when a major stressor caused similar symptoms, and did they improve once that stressor was over?

No, I've never gone through a major, overwhelming stressor like this in the past. I don't really have a previous experience to compare it to, since my life was pretty stable and predictable before my mom's stroke.
Have these symptoms caused you to miss work, make major mistakes, or struggle to take care of basic responsibilities at home because of the stress?

Yes, I had a dangerous near-miss safety incident at the shop because I was distracted thinking about my mom's meds, and my supervisor warned me about my attitude with coworkers. I also feel like I'm constantly dropping balls at home and have completely stopped participating in my usual church and truck club activities because I'm just so overwhelmed.
Have you ever had any similar episodes of feeling overwhelmed, sad, or unable to cope before this situation with your mom's stroke, even during other stressful times in your life?
No, I have never felt this way before. I've always been able to handle my life and routine normally, and I've never had issues coping with stress until my mom's stroke. This is completely new for me.
Have your symptoms been present continuously for less than 6 months, or have they lasted 6 months or longer?
They've been going on for less than six months. It’s been about four months now, starting right after my mom had her stroke and I suddenly had to become her main caregiver.
Have your symptoms started to improve at all as you’ve gotten more used to the caregiving situation, or are they still ongoing at the same level?

No, they haven't improved at all and are still ongoing at the same intense level. I feel just as overwhelmed as I did in the beginning because the caregiving demands haven't let up. I really think things will only start to get better once my mom's condition stabilizes or she doesn't need this level of constant care.
Have you noticed any improvement in your symptoms at all, or do they only seem tied to the ongoing caregiving stress and expected to ease once that stress ends?

No, I haven't seen any improvement yet because the caregiving demands are still constant. I believe my symptoms are entirely tied to this stress, and once my mom's health stabilizes or she doesn't need this level of hands-on care, I expect I'll be able to get back to my normal routine and stop feeling so strung out.
